_patch_meta.description: Stage 2 (the surface as the unit, meaning in context) and stage 4 (built on the stage 3 observations, behaviours discovered, no claims) and stage 5 (pulls observations together; the subgroups fall away) as the researcher defined them on #2526 (2026-11-21). Programme flow, The analytical grouping, Claims and the narrative, The collection reading, and the glossary entry stage (collection reading).

record.heading: Programme flow
record.body:
The programme organises its work into three stages: **Base_data**, **Analysis** and **Publishing**. Each stage has its own live mechanism, governed by its own configuration. The database carries each stage's state, and work is taken up at the point the database shows it left off.

**Base_data** runs from the text of the Bible to the identification of the surfaces. It has three parts, each built on the one before.

*The text and its data.* Every verse of the Bible is taken from STEP Bible together with its Hebrew and Greek words, their Strong's identities, meanings and relations, and the verse's interlinear presentation is kept verbatim. The mechanical reading of each verse (`verse_lexical`) is derived once from it and records the verse's structural composition and nothing of what a word does for the inner being. This is built verse by verse, by book and range, before any collection exists, and it is complete before any collection is read. Collections play no part in how it is batched.

*The surfaces.* The English words and phrases of the ESV, each linked through its Strong's codes to the original words behind it, are the population the study draws on. The whole population is sorted, by deduction and likeness, into four surface groups: behaviour, inner_being_state, entity and other. The sorting is roughly nine in ten correct, by the researcher's assessment, within an accepted margin; the items placed wrongly are found in the deeper analysis and compensated for there. Its purpose is to make the reading of the inner being's working possible.

*The collections.* The surfaces of the first two groups are collated, by the likeness or relatedness of the behaviour they name, into collections. Each surface belongs to one collection, and through the Strong's code of its base it is connected with its verses, so that a collection carries the verses its surfaces occur in (Chapter 4).

*The engagement step.* A surface is sorted into its group by what it names, before its verses are read, and what it does in a verse is settled only by reading the verse. The engagement step, run on a collection before the collection is read, assesses each member surface in each verse it occurs in, by the role it takes there, and the surface's group then follows from the roles. A surface that is a characteristic in any of its verses is a behaviour, and the difference between its verses is carried by the observations of each verse and not by the group. A surface that is a characteristic in none but is a qualifier in some is an inner-being state. A surface with no inner-being role in any verse leaves the study group, and each such departure is raised as a question for the researcher. A surface judged to have no bearing in a verse is recorded as a silence with the role standalone, and those verses are reviewed again, so that a surface found on re-reading to have a significant role in conjunction with another surface is given that role. Everything the step assesses is inferential until the researcher confirms it. The roles are set out in Chapter 4, under the node.

**Analysis** reads the inner being's working from the verses of the collections. The objective is to read those verses and deduce from them how the inner being works. A whole collection cannot be read in one go: to understand both the lexical context of the words in a verse and the inner-being working of the many behaviours a verse or group of verses carries is not achievable in one pass. The work is therefore split into units, and the units are read in layers and in stages.

*The unit.* To make a collection digestible, its surfaces are grouped further into surface subgroups. The subgroup is the unit of reading. In this programme "surface group" means one of the four groups of the surfaces, and a group of the surfaces of one collection is a subgroup.

*The layers.* Each layer deposits its findings as observations, so that they are available to the next layer, and each collection is digested into observations of lexical meaning first and of the inner-being working afterwards. The subgroup is used first to complete the verse-lexical observations for its surfaces and their verses, then to complete the lexical observations for how its surfaces relate to one another and to the other words in those verses. The subgroups and the lexical observations they now have are then the input of the inner-being analysis: the behaviours are discovered from analysing those observations, with only occasional reading back into the verses, and the observations for the elements of each behaviour are set, for the subgroup, for the collection and across collections. In this layer the subgroup is read as a collection of the workings of its words: it often forms one behaviour, and the lexical variation of its surfaces becomes the dimensions of how the behaviour works. The surface groups fall away in stage 5. Each cycle is a layer; each builds on the one before and uses its results. The lexical layers and the inner-being layer are separate processes and never run together, a step closes before the next opens, and every aspect a step demands is answered by an observation with its nodes, or by a recorded none with its reason. The steps the configuration holds, with what each asks, reads and leaves, are set out in Chapter 6, in the section 'The collection reading'; the rules that govern the observation and the node are in the configuration, and the section on the node in Chapter 4 describes how a node ties an observation to the text.

*The stages.* The configuration numbers the work of Analysis as five stages. The table gives, for each, what it is, the unit it works on and where it stands.

| Stage | What it is | The unit | Where it stands |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Lexical analysis of the words | Each word of a collection, a surface with its lettered Strong's code, is read in its verses and each sense the verses give it is recorded. Lexical only; the relations between words are base data and are not analysed here. | The word: one row of the ledger for each. A word whose occurrences are all function words (preposition, particle, pronoun, article, suffix and the like) has no row of its own, except a negator and a connective. | Built and tested. The first run on the first collection, thought, was withdrawn when the step was redesigned to record one observation for each sense a word has in its verses. The redesigned step has been run on 10 of the 177 words of thought; 167 stand open. The step is run for each collection, thought first. |
| 2. Grouping of the surfaces | The four surface groups, the collections, and the subgroups within a collection. The subgroups are judged from the meaning of their surfaces in context: the surface (the ESV word) is the unit and is placed whole in one subgroup, a word family is the default gathering, and a surface may carry a hidden meaning in the different Strong's codes used for it. Membership of the collection is taken as given. The subgroups state nothing of the inner being; a concept comes into play only in stage 4. | The surface within its collection: placed whole in a subgroup, or, where plainly not a member, set aside with its reason. | The surface groups and the collections are made. The grouping tools were rebuilt on the surface as the unit and tested (2026-11-21, #2526). No subgroup stands on a real collection: the method that formed them for the first collection judged each Strong's code on its own and is withdrawn, and the subgroups are formed again when collection processing starts, after stage 1. |
| 3. Verse-lexical observations | For each subgroup: its meaning (step 1.1), its enrichment from the Strong's codes of its surfaces (step 1.2), and what stands with it in the verses (step 2.1: pairings, qualifiers, entities, direction, the relation between subgroups, a double meaning). Lexical only. | The subgroup: every row is keyed to it. | Built in the application; never run. |
| 4. Inner-being analysis | The inner-being observations. The subgroups of a collection and the stage 3 observations on them are the input; the behaviours are discovered from analysing those observations, with only occasional reading back into the base data. Stage 4 articulates and sets the observations for all the elements of the behaviour, the building blocks, and formulates no claim. The lexical variation of stage 3 (the different codes, forms and uses of a surface) becomes the dimensions of how a behaviour works. | The subgroup's stage 3 observations (step 3.1), then the collection, where the behaviours are discovered (step 3.2), then across collections (step 3.3). A subgroup often forms one behaviour but need not. | Required. Redesigned and built (2026-11-21, #2528 and #2526) as steps 3.1 (the elements of each subgroup), 3.2 (the behaviours of the collection) and 3.3 (the working across collections) of the layered reading. Each finding rests on named observations; a reading back to a verse is recorded with its reason; every observation is rested on or declared with a reason. Its first form, a row for each subgroup and verse, was replaced the same day. It has not yet been run on any collection. |
| 5. Claims | Pulls the stage 4 observations together into behaviour statements, and updates the claims register. It discovers no building block (that is stage 4), and the surface groups fall away in it: stage 5 receives observations only. | The observations. | Not decided. |

That numbering was set before the order of the layers above was stated, and it is read against it. How the two are aligned is open, in particular where the grouping into subgroups falls in relation to the lexical analysis of the words: as the configuration holds it, the analysis of the words is a step that needs no grouping and closes before the grouping is read, while the researcher's order makes the subgroup the base unit of the first layer as well.

*What the subgroup is for.* The researcher's reasoning, recorded when the layered reading was defined, is this. A collection holds words that carry one concept in many forms, and its subgroups are the concepts inside it: surfaces of like meaning, such as the derivatives of one word that travel together. Gathering them lets a finding be stated once for the concept and not once for each surface, while the verses of every surface travel with it through the nodes, so that an observation made for the subgroup is found for each of its verses. In stage 3 the subgroup is the unit every observation is keyed to: its meaning, its enrichment from the Strong's codes of its surfaces, which links it to its usage in the verses, and then what stands with it in the verses, whether subgroups relate or are used interchangeably, the qualifiers, the entities and the direction the text states. Reading the subgroup also tests the grouping: where a grouping is found wrong it is reformed. In stage 4 the subgroups and their observations are the input from which the behaviours are discovered. A word is not analysed alone in the claims reading; it is bound with its partner, the characteristic, or it is excluded, and a word wrongly included in a collection is moved to entity or other and the move is processed, so that the completeness tests continue to hold. The lexical layers prepare the base data for the formulation of claims.

*Volume.* The collection is the unit of a sitting of the tools: every step of the layered reading is opened, pulled, recorded and checked for one named collection, and every gate is per collection. The grouping of a collection is one pass over its surfaces, one row for each surface, judged from its meaning in context. The analysis of the words is the largest part of the work, one row for each word of the collection. Its pull writes every open row at once and limits only the evidence shown for a row, which is capped at a configured number of occurrences; the filled file is checked as a whole and written in one transaction, and a problem anywhere in it refuses the whole file. A row stays open until it is recorded and validated, so a collection can be left partly answered and the next pull returns what is left. The configuration sets no order in which the collections are taken, no number of rows for one sitting and no rule for resuming other than the open state of the ledger. A job that runs longer than a few minutes is started outside the working session, with a log, so that it can be checked, stopped and resumed.

*Gates.* A step closes only when every row it demands is answered by an observation with its nodes, or by a recorded none with its reason, and validated by the check; the next step does not open before it. The steps of stage 3 do not open until the grouping of the collection is finished: every surface placed or set aside with its reason, and every subgroup holding a surface. The closure of stage 3 is a gate for the collection, and stage 4 is not opened until stage 3 is complete; this is read as every step of stage 3 for the collection. A stage that finds an earlier observation wrong does not correct it in place: the case returns to the earlier stage, where a row answered again withdraws its earlier observation with its reason.

*What stage 3 leaves.* When stage 3 is complete a collection holds, for each subgroup, its meaning and its Strong's enrichment, which is never a none; a pairing for each partner collection with which it shares at least three verses; a qualifier, an entity and the direction the text states, where the verses show them; a relation for each pair of subgroups that share at least three verses; and a double meaning for each surface that carries two or more Strong's codes. Each is an observation with its nodes, each node carrying its verse, word, surface, collection and subgroup, and the set is the complete verse-lexical account of the collection. Stage 4 reads that account. What each of these observations states is what the dictionary, the verses and the stored structure show: the grammatical qualifier is a stage 3 observation, and what the qualifier gives the behaviour in place is a stage 4 observation.

*Fallout.* Some surfaces, words and aspects are not analysed, and the programme states what is done about each.

| What is not analysed | What is done |
|---|---|
| Surfaces of the groups entity and other | They are not members of any collection. They enter the study as the words that stand with a collection's surfaces, as nodes of the observation that covers them. A verse that holds only such surfaces is out of scope and is not touched. |
| A word wrongly included in a collection | It is found at any stage and moved by the procedure for changing a collection, and the move is processed so that the step reopens. |
| Surfaces wrongly sorted into the four groups, unjudged or set aside | They are found in the deeper analysis and compensated for there; the step that records them is not yet defined. |
| A surface plainly not a member of the collection in meaning | It is set aside in the grouping with its reason and moved out by the procedure for changing a collection. |
| A function word | It is read with its unit and has no row of its own, except a negator and a connective. |
| A qualifier, an entity or a double meaning that is not present | A recorded none with its reason, where the step allows it. |
| An aspect of a Strong's code that the verses do not carry | It is not a conflict or an error; no observation need focus on a meaning that is not about the inner being. |
| Surfaces not yet placed in a subgroup | They stop stage 3 from opening for the collection until they are placed or set aside. |

*What the inner-being layer reads.* Stage 4 reads how the inner being works from the observations of stage 3. The researcher's placement is settled: how the inner being is read belongs to this layer, and what the readings show together, how workings are grained and linked, how states and transitions behave and how a characteristic emerges, belongs to the claims, where the answers are discovered from the observations. The order of the study is to finish reading the inner-being surface groups into observations and then to formulate the claims. The researcher has stated what is read: behaviour is not only acts or operations but also states and conditions, for example sin, righteousness, life and death; it has qualifiers that define it; and a characteristic such as anger or love is not a thing and is not defined in advance, being known only by inference from the collection of behaviours, processes, actions and movements that give it substance. The programme's record of how the working has been defined, from the first working definition to the layers, shows the same few parts recurring under different names: the bearer and the seat, the behaviour in its three forms of act, state and movement, the qualifiers, the source and the object, the effect, the link to other workings, the expression or what is hidden behind it, and the context of the passage. The lexical layers hold a home for few of these, and the inner-being layer needs one for the bearer, the state of a being, the transition, the effect, the expression, the context and the link. This is the record's reading and it is inferential until the researcher confirms it. The study has also defined the interventions that a reading triggers: read beyond the verse, in its passage, genre and speaker; read outward from the verse and not inward from a question; check the original; reclassify a word whose role in this verse is not the one its collection gives it; do not force a meaning and never close on 'not X'; record a discovery outside the verse separately. They are carried into the layered reading as the interventions that every stage 4 row prompts (cfg_setting layer.interventions). The test applied to every result is whether it is sensible, reasonable and defensible. The rules of this reading are already held in the configuration: nine items explored for every characteristic (meaning, role, polarity, object, enactment, party with its route, circumstance, operation with its chain, and a flag), eight kinds of finding, the node roles, the method rules of the reading step on how a verse is read and how a finding is written, and sixteen nuance pointers. Stage 4 is built from them: what stages 1 and 3 now do is taken out, the rest is placed on the collection, the subgroup and the ledger, and the level across subgroups and collections and the interventions listed above are added. Every finding of a stage 4 row rests on named observations and carries nodes with the role the reading gives each occurrence; an occurrence outside the observations it rests on is allowed only with a recorded read-back (the verse and the reason), and a word that holds nothing for the inner being takes the role standalone.

*Role in the inner-being layer.* The role a word has in a verse is what the inner-being layer reads by. It is judged for each occurrence, from the verse and against what the verse is about, and never taken from the cluster tag, from the collection or from the part the word usually plays: the same word can be a characteristic in one verse and a qualifier in another, and a word that has no inner-being role in a verse is not forced into one (the node, in Chapter 4, sets out the roles). Two consequences are the researcher's. The role is the filter of the deeper reading: the deeper reading of the verses in the next phase is filtered on the role of the words, so that the study is not contaminated by words that have little or no bearing on the inner being; where that filter sits in the claims phase is not yet defined, and it is not built. And a role is never a verdict: a verse or an item is never closed as 'only a qualifier' or 'no bearing'. What is recorded is what the verse is, with every significance it carries, since a verse often carries two or three and none is dropped because it was not the one asked about.

*The claims.* Claims are formulated from the inner-being observations. The formulation of claims is not yet decided. The claims that exist come from an earlier method and are not yet tied to the collections; each is to be cross-linked to its collection and re-evaluated against the observations.

**Publishing** is the production of the essays and output that carry the results: the narrative, held in the database as chapters and sections, and exported for its readers.

**Where the programme stands.** The base data is complete for the Bible: every verse, its original-language data and its mechanical reading. The surfaces are sorted into the four groups, with a small remainder not yet judged, and the surfaces of behaviour and inner_being_state are gathered into collections. The reading, which is the centre of the study, has not properly started. The layered reading is built, and it was opened on the first collection, thought, but no collection has completed a stage, no subgroup stands, and no stage 3 observation exists. The observations in the database were made by earlier methods (documents captured, readings by cluster, by strand and by phase) and are held as gathered rows; each is re-read into the layers collection by collection, and one that cannot be made to comply with the rules of the observation and the node is retired with its nodes as a soft delete with its reason. The inner-being layer is required and is built, from the inner-being reading rules the configuration holds, as steps 3.1 to 3.3 of the layered reading, but it has not been run on any collection; the claims are not decided. The account, the claims and the narrative, is a complete draft assembled from readings made under earlier units, so it cannot yet be said to rest on the collections. The process control, with its escalation record, compliance check and session close, is operating. The current counts are held in the reports and not in this prose.

**What stands unsolved.** These gaps are recognised in the record and are not closed.
- No check of content exists before a stage closes. The structural checks of the application have passed while the content was wrong, and each content gap found so far was found by the researcher reading one case by hand.
- No independent control of completeness operates on the study's universe. The earlier controls, a comparison with the primary lexica, a lemma inventory and a candidate net, were each built and retired.
- The surfaces judged are those reached through the Strong's codes that the earlier cluster method allocated. A large share of the occurrences in the text lie on other codes and reach the study only as words that stand with member surfaces. Whether that boundary stays or widens is the researcher's to decide.
- The layered design has not been run through a stage on any collection, so it has not met the test at which an earlier reading technique failed, consistency at scale.
- The recorders of the layered reading were audited against the rules after the first run failed and not before it.

**What is not yet defined.** The programme states what it does not yet know, so that it is not mistaken for settled.
- The order in which the collections are taken, and the size of one sitting of the reading, are not set.
- How behaviours are found in stage 4 when they do not coincide with a subgroup (one that crosses subgroups, or a part of one): the first runs will show the cases.
- The alignment of the configuration's stage numbering with the order of the layers above.
- How the working of the inner being is depicted systematically and checked, and how a reading is kept consistent from one read to the next: the stage 4 steps are built and have not been run, so what they leave is not yet known to be enough for this.
- The grain of the inner-being reading. A node is an occurrence of a word, while a working is a relation among occurrences; how one working across several nodes is one record is not stated. The unit of a batch of the inner-being reading, and how the nuances and variances of a working are handled when the same word works differently in different verses, are also not stated.
- The filter of the deeper reading by role: which verses and words go on to the deeper reading because the word has an inner-being role in them, and where in the claims phase that is applied. The roles of the nodes written by earlier methods are not all set (Chapter 4, the node), and setting them has been handed to the collection reading.
- The formulation of claims from the inner-being observations.
- How the chapters of the narrative follow the collections beyond the chapter on the inner being at work, which is built by collection. The researcher has called one chapter for each collection enormous and has said that the groupings are not yet known and should come from the claims; the rules that name the collection as the chapter would then be amended.
- How the per-cluster science reviews held as reference files are used in the claims reading; loading them into a reading was never built.
- The surfaces that were sorted wrongly, not yet judged or set aside: the step that records them, whether a surface rightly in a collection but set aside is read afterwards, whether a pairing or a relation of fewer than three shared verses is meant to be left unread, and whether the surfaces that have no group set are in the collections or out of them.

The programme's methods have changed materially over its life, as its record shows, and this section describes what operates now.

record.heading: The analytical grouping: collections and subgroups
record.body:
The programme's analytical grouping is the collection and, within it, the subgroup. A collection gathers surfaces of like or related behaviour (Chapter 2). A subgroup is a group of the surfaces of one collection, made so that the collection can be read in units: the subgroup is the unit of reading, and its surfaces are read together in each layer. The verses of a subgroup's surfaces travel with it through the nodes, so that an observation made for the subgroup is found for each of its verses. The unit that is grouped is the surface, placed whole in one subgroup; the subgroup is judged from the meaning of its surfaces in context, and a surface may carry a hidden meaning in the different Strong's codes used for it. The concept tables of an earlier method are retired and the collection takes their place. The method that grouped the surfaces of the first collection did not serve the purpose the subgroups are for and is withdrawn; the subgroups are formed again when collection processing starts.

The readings of a collection are recorded in the observation tables. `ib_observation` holds one finding, with its stage, its kind (for example term, face, group, enrichment, pairing or relation), its text and its status. `ib_node` holds the occurrences the observation applies to (the previous section). `ib_observation_change` keeps every change to an observation with its reason, so that a withdrawal is a soft delete that can be explained. `collection_layer_item` is the ledger of the layered reading: one row for each aspect a step of the reading demands for a collection, which is closed by an observation with its nodes or by a recorded none with its reason, and is then validated by the check.

The values of the stage of an observation are `lexical` (stage 1), `layer-1` and `layer-2` (stage 3) and `layer-3` (stage 4, the inner-being analysis). Observations made by earlier methods are kept as the history of those methods; a live observation must comply with the rules of the observation and the node, and one that cannot be revived to comply is retired with its nodes as a soft delete with its reason.

The reading process of the app (`Reading.ps1`) takes a reading of one scope through three gates (recorded, synergised, published) and is being aligned to collections.

record.heading: Claims and the narrative
record.body:
The account of the programme is built from the observations upward through two tables of claims and a narrative, all in `iba.db`. `narrative_claim` holds each **claim**: a statement derived from sources, the verses and, later, the science reading, that goes beyond their mere text, held in its own plain wording. A quotation is not a claim. `narrative_claim_source` holds the sources of each claim and its verdict against the wording of the original essay: stands, restated, widened, corrected or new. `narrative_claim_telling` records how the narrative tells each claim: in full, in part or by pointer. Each claim is therefore traceable to its sources and to the place in the narrative where it is told.

`narrative_chapter` is the authority for which chapters exist, their order and their purpose. `narrative_section` holds the sections of each chapter, whose text is a block; `narrative_citation` holds the citations and `narrative_update` the record of updates to the narrative. The chapter files are exports from the database; the database is the home of the narrative.

The claims are formulated from the observations in stage 5 of the reading, which is not yet decided. What is established is that a claim is bound to the observations and nodes that found it, and that the claims of a collection are formulated after its inner-being analysis (stage 4), which is built and has not yet been run. Stage 5 pulls the observations of stage 4 together into behaviour statements; it discovers no building block (that is stage 4), and the surface subgroups fall away there, because all the analysis of the subgroups and their verses is carried into stage 5 as observations. The existing claims come from an earlier method and are not yet cross-linked to the collections; that cross-linking, and the re-evaluation of each claim against the observations, belongs to the work of stages 4 and 5. Larger claims are not made before the smaller claims on which they rest.

record.heading: The collection reading
record.body:
The collection is read through the layered reading, run with `Collection-Build.ps1` (`LayerOpen`, `LayerPull`, `LayerRecord` and `LayerCheck`) over the steps and items of `cfg_setting layer.reading`. A step is opened only when the previous one is closed. As the configuration holds it, the lexical analysis of the words (step S1) closes before the grouping of the surfaces is read, and the grouping is finished before the steps that follow; the order of Chapter 2 governs, and the alignment of the two is open. The rows each step demands are the ledger `collection_layer_item`, derived from the data, and each is answered by an observation with its nodes or by a recorded none with its reason. The stages and steps are described in Chapter 2, and the rules that govern them are configuration rows, delivered at the first use of the routine. The evidence on which a collection is read, its member occurrences, its sense and its pairings, is produced by the collection evidence report from the tables.

**The steps the configuration holds.** The ledger of the reading holds four steps today, each opened for one collection only when the one before it is closed. For each, the table gives what it asks, what it reads, how it is done and what it leaves.

| Step | What it asks | What it reads | How it is done | What it leaves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1, the words | In the verses where each word of the collection stands, what does it mean in each, as the verse itself shows it? | The occurrences of the collection by surface and lettered Strong's code (`verse_lexical`), the sense tree, LSJ and Mounce entries of the code, the meaning prompts of the question catalogue, and the observations already recorded for those occurrences. | One ledger row for each word, except a word whose occurrences are all function words. The open rows are pulled into a working file with their evidence, Claude reads and fills each row, the record step checks the whole file and writes it in one transaction, and the check validates each answered row. | One observation for each sense the verses give the word, with the occurrences it holds for (every occurrence in some sense); an occurrence whose sense departs from the usual one is a face observation. Each has nodes of the role `lexical`. |
| 1.1, the groups | What do the surfaces of this subgroup mean, as the surfaces show it in their verses? | The subgroups of the collection, each surface placed in one or set aside with its reason, and the lexicon entries of their codes. Opens only when S1 is closed and every surface is placed or set aside. | One ledger row for each subgroup, taken through the same pull, fill, record and check. | One observation for each subgroup stating the meaning its surfaces share, with a node for each occurrence of its surfaces. |
| 1.2, the Strong's enrichment | What do the Strong's codes of this subgroup say, and does the grouping stand against them? | The lexicon entries of the subgroup's codes. | One ledger row for each subgroup. | One observation for each subgroup giving a short definition from the lexicon and naming the codes that link it to its usage. |
| 2.1, the pairings | What do the other words of the verses show with this subgroup: the words of other collections that stand with it, qualifiers and the words they reach, entities, the direction the text states, the relation between subgroups, a double meaning? | The typed pairings of the evidence report for the collection, and the thresholds the configuration sets for how many shared verses a pairing or a relation needs. | One ledger row for each pairing, qualifier, entity, direction, relation or double meaning the data demands; a recorded none with its reason is allowed where the step permits it. | Observations of the kinds pairing, relation and face, with nodes for the member occurrences and the partner occurrences. |

Every observation these steps leave states what the dictionary, the verses and the stored structure show, and carries no inner-being role. The inner-being layer (stage 4) follows in three steps, each closed before the next opens and none opened before stage 3 is closed for the collection. Its input is the subgroups and the stage 3 observations on them; the behaviours are discovered from analysing those observations, with only occasional reading back into the verses, and every reading back is recorded with the verse and the reason. It sets observations and formulates no claim. Step 3.1, the elements of the subgroups: for each subgroup, the findings (operation, polarity, object, enactment, party, circumstance, the role and dimension a variation gives, the chain, a flag) that its stage 3 observations show, each a finding that rests on named observations by a traced node and carries nodes with their roles; every stage 3 observation of the subgroup is rested on or declared not used with its reason. Step 3.2, the behaviours of the collection: the behaviours are discovered from the element observations, each recorded as a discovery flag that names the behaviour and gathers its elements by traced nodes and makes no claim about it, and what relates elements across subgroups is recorded; every element is gathered or declared not gathered; a collection that shows no behaviour is recorded as none with its reason. Step 3.3, across collections: for each subgroup and partner collection that share at least three verses, how they work together, resting on observations of the steps below. The rules of the inner-being reading that the configuration holds (the observation items, the kinds of finding, the node roles, the method rules of the reading step and the nuance pointers) are its base; the interventions of the reading are prompted on every row. It is built and has not yet been run on any collection.

record.heading: stage (collection reading)
record.body:
[DEFINITION] The five stages of the reading of a collection, as the researcher defined them (2026-11-15): stage 1, the lexical analysis of the words (each word in its verses, lexical only; the relations between the words are base data and are not analysed); stage 2, the grouping of the surfaces by their meaning (the four surface groups, the collections of behaviour and inner_being_state, the subgroups within a collection judged from the meaning of their surfaces in context, each surface placed whole); stage 3, the verse-lexical observations (layer 1 step 2 and layer 2, verse-lexical only); stage 4, the inner-being analysis: the behaviours discovered from the stage 3 observations and the observations set for their elements, no claim formulated; stage 5, the claim formulation, which pulls the stage 4 observations together into behaviour statements, and the update of the claims register, not yet decided. Stages 1 to 3 are lexical work and carry nothing of the inner being.

[BACKGROUND] Held in cfg_setting layer.reading (the steps S1, 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 and, for stage 4, 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3) and the ib_observation.stage values lexical, layer-1, layer-2 and layer-3. Stage 4 is built (2026-11-21, #2528) and has not yet been run on a collection. The four stages of the retired cluster pipeline (verse-reading, char-subgroup, char-reading, char-answers) are replaced by these and their observations are gathered rows.
